vocabulary_concerns: “Income beyond reimbursement” must mean any income other than the specified reimbursement, not merely positive net profit or receipts exceeding total expenses. The permitted reimbursement is expressly for operating expenses and from the family.

“Genuine single family office” remains a judgment-dependent classification. Q1 says the Ordinance does not define family or family office; Q2 uses “typically” and “often,” which do not impose mandatory corporate ownership or structural requirements.
“Profit objective,” profit capability, realized income and continuity are distinct concepts. The source lists case-specific considerations without supplying a rule for combining them.

“Not being run as a business” and “carrying on a business in Hong Kong” should not become globally interchangeable with an income test. The parenthetical supports, at most, the bounded interpretation being examined.

“Should not in the ordinary course” expresses qualified guidance, and regulatory intent is not an unconditional statutory exemption. TRUE means antecedent satisfaction only; FALSE does not establish a licensing obligation.
The same-period assumption and UNKNOWN/CONFLICT rules are modeling conventions, not rules stated in the FAQ. The source supplies no precise accounting period or timing test.
